//test-timeout: 420s, per test. Chosen on this project's four-core Raspberry Pi under deliberate heavy load, because that is the machine that loses these races (issue #53); an idle CI runner does the whole suite in ~25s. Measured there at load average 25, the slowest single test took 54.3s and a bare `covey stop` against an empty port took 30.9s, so the 60s this started as would have been a flake, not a bound. 420s is ~8x the slowest measured test, and it also clears the sum of the inner bounds in that test — a 60s daemon start, a 150s CLI run, a 30s wait for an exit — so a real fault is named by the bound that knows what went wrong rather than by this one. Too tight is a flake on slow hardware, which is worse than the hang it replaces. Note what it does not cover: a test file whose tests have all finished but whose process cannot exit. Node bounds a test, not a lingering process — measured, an unfixed run with --test-timeout=30000 still ran 238916ms. That is packages/daemon/test/daemons.ts's job.

scripts.check: pnpm run check:age && pnpm run check:crate-age && pnpm run typecheck && pnpm test
